![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14246252/assets/98b9df96585a5e7067f229ed85a2e60309fbc56865d9bdf61d98aed68ac70ac2.png)

The point $A$ with coordinates $(4,\operatorname{ln}⁡4)$ lies on the curve $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ and the point ${A}^{′}$ with coordinates $(1,\operatorname{ln}⁡4)$ lies on the curve $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(ax),$ shown above. What is the value of $a?$
question.worked_solution:
The graph of $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(ax)$ can be obtained from $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ by a horizontal stretch of scale factor $\frac{1}{a}.$ 

From the diagram, we deduce that under such a transformation, the point $(4,\operatorname{ln}⁡4)$ that lies on $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ becomes 

$$
(\frac{1}{a}\cdot 4,\operatorname{ln}⁡4)=(1,\operatorname{ln}⁡4)
$$

which lies on $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(ax).$ 

Therefore, $a=4.$
